examples.en: I ate raw sliced fish by the sea on the weekend.
The fresher the raw fish is here, the better it tastes.
Try dipping the raw fish in spicy red pepper sauce.

examples.ko: 저는 생선회를 못 먹어서 구이를 시켰어요.
examples.en: I can't eat raw fish, so I ordered grilled fish.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 생선회 한 접시에 얼마예요?
examples.en: How much is one plate of raw fish at this restaurant?

examples.ko: 생선회랑 같이 나오는 매운탕도 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: The spicy fish stew that comes with the raw fish is really good too.

explain: 보통은 줄여서 '회'라고 많이 말해요. '회를 먹다', '회를 뜨다'처럼 쓰고, 식당에서도 '회 한 접시 주세요'라고 하면 자연스러워요. 상추나 깻잎에 싸 먹거나 초고추장, 쌈장과 함께 먹는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: People often shorten it to just '회'. You say '회를 먹다' (eat raw fish) or '회를 뜨다' (slice raw fish), and at a restaurant '회 한 접시 주세요' sounds natural. It is often wrapped in lettuce or perilla leaves, or eaten with spicy red pepper sauce or ssamjang.

examples.en: Sera's birthday party is the evening after tomorrow.

examples.ko: 아이 생일잔치에 친구들을 열 명 초대했어요.
examples.en: We invited ten friends to the child's birthday party.
We decided to hold Grandma's birthday party at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 생일잔치를 집에서 하면 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: If you hold a birthday party at home, there is a lot to prepare.

examples.ko: 어제 생일잔치에서 케이크를 두 조각이나 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate as many as two pieces of cake at the birthday party yesterday.

examples.ko: 생일잔치 때 입을 옷을 아직 못 골랐어요.
examples.en: I haven't picked out what to wear to the birthday party yet.

explain: '잔치'는 음식을 차리고 여럿이 모이는 자리라서 '생일 파티'보다 조금 전통적인 느낌이 있어요. 젊은 사람들은 보통 '생일 파티'라고 말해요. 같은 식으로 '돌잔치', '환갑잔치'도 써요.
explain_en: '잔치' suggests a gathering with food laid out for many guests, so it feels a bit more traditional than '생일 파티'. Younger people usually say '생일 파티'. The same word appears in '돌잔치' (first birthday feast) and '환갑잔치' (60th birthday feast).

examples.en: On New Year's morning, I bow to my grandmother.
After you bow, the adults give you New Year's money.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 설날마다 친척 집을 돌며 세배해요.
examples.en: Every New Year's Day, my family goes around to relatives' houses to bow.
The children lined up and bowed to their parents.

examples.ko: 어른께 세배할 때는 한복을 입는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: People often wear hanbok when bowing to elders.

examples.ko: 올해는 멀어서 직접 세배하지 못하고 전화를 드렸어요.
examples.en: This year it was too far, so I couldn't bow in person and called instead.

explain: 설날에 어른께 큰절을 하며 새해 인사를 드리는 것을 말하고, '세배를 하다'로도 많이 써요. 받는 쪽 어른은 '새해 복 많이 받아'라고 덕담을 하고 세뱃돈을 주기도 해요. 어른께는 '세배 드리다'라고 높여 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: This is the New Year greeting where you bow deeply to elders, and '세배를 하다' is just as common. The elder usually replies with good wishes like '새해 복 많이 받아' and may give New Year's money. To be more polite toward the elder, you can also say '세배 드리다'.

examples.ko: 손녀딸이 오면 할머니는 항상 용돈을 주세요.
examples.en: Whenever her granddaughter comes, Grandma always gives her pocket money.
Our granddaughter has already become an elementary school student.
Grandfather calls his granddaughter every day.
I took a photo holding my granddaughter at the park.
This outfit is a gift for my granddaughter.

examples.ko: 옆집 할머니는 손녀딸 자랑을 자주 하세요.
examples.en: The grandmother next door often brags about her granddaughter.

explain: '손녀'와 같은 사람을 가리키는데, '딸'이 붙어서 더 다정한 느낌이 나요. 할머니, 할아버지가 말할 때 특히 잘 어울려요. 남자 손주는 '손자'이고, 손자와 손녀를 함께 '손주'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It refers to the same person as '손녀', but the added '딸' gives it a warmer, more affectionate feel, especially when grandparents talk. A grandson is '손자', and grandchildren together are called '손주'.

examples.ko: 이 니트는 세탁기 말고 손빨래해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hand-wash this knit, not use the washing machine.
Hand-washing is hard work, but it damages clothes less.
I just quickly hand-washed a few pairs of socks.
Winter blankets are too heavy to wash by hand.
Hand-wash expensive blouses in cold water.
I heard people used to do all the laundry by hand.

explain: '손빨래를 하다'와 '손빨래하다' 둘 다 자연스러워요. 세탁기로 빠는 것과 달리 손으로 직접 빠는 것이라서, 옷 라벨에 '손세탁'이라고 쓰여 있을 때가 있어요. 맡겨서 빠는 건 '세탁소에 맡기다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Both '손빨래를 하다' and '손빨래하다' sound natural. It contrasts with washing by machine, and clothing labels sometimes say '손세탁' (hand wash). Sending clothes out is '세탁소에 맡기다' (leave at the laundry).

examples.en: I received a small wallet as a gift.

examples.ko: 손지갑에 카드 두 장과 동전을 넣었어요.
examples.en: I put two cards and some coins in my small wallet.
I can't find my small wallet in my bag.
I find a small wallet more convenient than a big one.
I lost my small wallet, so I went to the police station.

examples.ko: 이 손지갑은 동전 넣는 칸이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: This small wallet has a separate compartment for coins.

explain: 지갑은 모양과 크기에 따라 '장지갑', '반지갑', '카드지갑', '동전지갑'처럼 나눠 불러요. 손지갑은 이름 그대로 손에 쥐거나 가방에 쏙 넣을 만한 작은 지갑일 때 써요. '지갑을 잃어버리다', '지갑을 꺼내다'처럼 쓰면 돼요.
explain_en: Wallets are named by shape and size, such as '장지갑' (long wallet), '반지갑' (bifold), '카드지갑' (card holder) and '동전지갑' (coin purse). '손지갑' fits a small wallet you can hold in your hand or tuck into a bag. Use it like '지갑을 잃어버리다' (lose a wallet) or '지갑을 꺼내다' (take out a wallet).

examples.en: A shoulder bag goes on your shoulder, so your hands are free.
I want to buy a new shoulder bag.
Will my laptop fit in this shoulder bag?

examples.ko: 이 숄더백은 끈 길이를 조절할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The strap length of this shoulder bag is adjustable.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 숄더백보다 배낭이 편해요.
examples.en: For travel, a backpack is more comfortable than a shoulder bag.
A friend gave me a shoulder bag as a birthday present.

explain: 가방은 '들다'가 아니라 '메다'와 함께 써서 '숄더백을 메다'라고 해요. 몸을 대각선으로 가로질러 메는 가방은 '크로스백'이라고 따로 불러요. 등에 지는 가방은 '백팩'이나 '배낭'이에요.
explain_en: With a shoulder bag you use the verb '메다' (carry on the shoulder) instead of '들다' (hold), so '숄더백을 메다'. A bag worn diagonally across the body is called a '크로스백' (crossbody bag). A bag carried on your back is a '백팩' or '배낭'.

examples.ko: 병원에서 낸 수술비가 생각보다 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The surgery cost I paid at the hospital was more than I expected.

examples.ko: 수술비는 보험으로 일부 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get part of the surgery cost back through insurance.
I cashed in my savings account to raise the money for my parents' surgery.
I asked the hospital how much the surgery would cost.

examples.ko: 아버지 수술비 때문에 걱정이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: I'm really worried because of my father's surgery costs.
You have to pay the surgery fee before being discharged.

explain: '수술비가 들다·나오다', '수술비를 내다·마련하다'처럼 함께 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. 병원에서 쓰는 돈 전체는 '병원비'라고 하고, '치료비'는 치료에 드는 돈이에요. 같은 방식으로 '입원비', '검사비'도 있어요.
explain_en: It pairs with fixed verbs: '수술비가 들다/나오다' (the cost comes to) and '수술비를 내다/마련하다' (pay/raise the cost). '병원비' covers hospital money overall, while '치료비' is the cost of treatment. In the same pattern there are '입원비' (hospitalization) and '검사비' (testing).

examples.ko: 이 영상은 하루 만에 수십만 명이 봤어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of thousands of people watched this video in one day.

examples.ko: 수십만 원짜리 가방을 큰마음 먹고 샀어요.
examples.en: I made up my mind and bought a bag worth several hundred thousand won.
I heard hundreds of thousands gathered at that singer's concert.

examples.ko: 수십만 개가 팔렸는데도 재고가 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Even though hundreds of thousands were sold, there is still stock left.

examples.ko: 한 달 월세가 수십만 원이라 부담돼요.
examples.en: The monthly rent is hundreds of thousands of won, so it's a burden.
Roughly several hundred thousand people live in this city.

explain: 정확한 숫자를 모르거나 어림해서 말할 때 '수십만 명', '수십만 원'처럼 단위와 함께 써요. 비슷한 말로 '수만', '수백만'이 있고, 말할 때는 '몇십만'이라고도 해요. 보통 뒤에 오는 단위와 띄어 써요.
explain_en: Use it with a counter like '수십만 명' or '수십만 원' when you don't know or are estimating the exact number. Similar words are '수만' (tens of thousands) and '수백만' (millions), and in speech people also say '몇십만'. It is normally written with a space before the counter.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 집 근처 스케이트장이 문을 열어요.
examples.en: In winter, the skating rink near my house opens.
I met my friends at the skating rink on the weekend.
How much is admission to the skating rink in front of City Hall?
The kids have fun at the rink even while falling down.
It takes about thirty minutes by subway to get to the skating rink.
There are too many people at the skating rink today.

explain: '스케이트를 타다'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 얼음 위에서 타는 곳이라서 '아이스링크'라고도 하고, 스포츠 경기용으로는 '빙상장'이라는 말도 써요. 가는 곳이니까 '스케이트장에 가다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Learn it together with '스케이트를 타다' (to skate). People also say '아이스링크', and '빙상장' is used for sports venues. Since it is a place you go to, say '스케이트장에 가다'.

examples.en: Every morning the school bus comes to the front of the apartment building.
My child missed the school bus, so I drove him.
What time does the school bus arrive at school?

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 스쿨버스로 통학하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: At our school, many students commute by school bus.
On the field trip day, we went by school bus.
I sang songs with my friend on the school bus.

explain: '통학버스'라는 말도 비슷하게 써요. 학원에서 아이들을 태우는 차는 보통 '학원 버스'라고 해요. '타다, 내리다, 놓치다'와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: '통학버스' (commuter bus for students) is used in a similar way. A bus that picks up kids for a private academy is usually called a '학원 버스'. It often goes with the verbs '타다' (ride), '내리다' (get off) and '놓치다' (miss).

examples.en: There are lots of persimmons in the yard of Grandma's country house.
Meals at a country house are simple, but you can feel the warmth.
At Chuseok, the whole family goes down to the country house.
After resting a few days at the country house, my body feels lighter.
The country house was old, so we fixed the roof anew.
Every vacation I go to the country house and play with my cousins.

explain: 서울에서 지방으로 갈 때는 '내려가다'를 써서 '시골집에 내려가다'라고 말해요. 부모님이나 조부모님이 사는 집이면 '고향집', '본가'라고도 해요. 명절 때 많이 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: When you go from Seoul out to the provinces, Koreans use '내려가다' (go down), as in '시골집에 내려가다'. If it is where your parents or grandparents live, you can also say '고향집' or '본가'. It comes up a lot around the holidays.

examples.en: There are ten pairs of shoes in the shoe cabinet.
The shoe cabinet next to the entrance is too narrow.
I tidied the shoe cabinet before the guests came.

examples.ko: 새 운동화를 신발장 맨 위 칸에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I put the new sneakers on the top shelf of the shoe cabinet.

examples.ko: 신발장 문이 안 닫혀서 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: The shoe cabinet door won't close, so I need to fix it.

examples.ko: 우리 집 신발장은 우산도 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Our shoe cabinet can hold umbrellas too.

explain: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗기 때문에 대부분 현관 쪽에 신발장이 있어요. 신발을 '넣다, 꺼내다, 정리하다'와 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '신발장'이라고 하면 충분히 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Korean homes have you take off shoes at the entrance, so the shoe cabinet is usually right there. It goes with verbs like '넣다' (put in), '꺼내다' (take out) and '정리하다' (tidy up). In daily speech, '신발장' is perfectly natural.

examples.ko: 엄마가 쌀가게에서 쌀 이십 킬로그램을 사 오셨어요.
examples.en: Mom bought twenty kilograms of rice at the rice shop.

examples.ko: 동네 쌀가게 아저씨가 집까지 배달해 주세요.
examples.en: The man at the neighborhood rice shop delivers to our house.

examples.ko: 이 쌀가게는 쌀 종류가 정말 다양해요.
examples.en: This rice shop has a really wide variety of rice.
I asked at the rice shop whether the new-harvest rice had come in.

examples.ko: 요즘은 쌀가게보다 인터넷으로 쌀을 많이 사요.
examples.en: These days people buy rice online more than at rice shops.

examples.ko: 시장 입구에 있던 쌀가게가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The rice shop at the market entrance has closed down.

explain: '쌀집'이라고도 해요. 요즘은 마트나 인터넷에서 쌀을 사는 사람이 많아서 동네 쌀가게는 예전보다 적어요. '쌀을 팔다·사다·배달하다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is also called '쌀집'. These days many people buy rice at supermarkets or online, so neighborhood rice shops are less common than before. It goes with '쌀을 팔다/사다/배달하다' (sell/buy/deliver rice).

examples.ko: 큰 포대의 쌀을 쌀통에 쏟아 넣었어요.
examples.en: I poured the rice from the big sack into the rice bin.
The rice bin was empty, so I ordered rice.

examples.ko: 쌀통 뚜껑을 닫지 않으면 벌레가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you don't close the rice bin lid, bugs will get in.
I placed a rice bin in the corner of the kitchen.

examples.ko: 쌀통에서 밥 지을 만큼 쌀을 퍼요.
examples.en: I scoop out as much rice as I need for cooking from the rice bin.
In summer, keep the rice bin in a cool place.

explain: 쌀을 퍼내는 동작은 '푸다'라서 '쌀을 퍼요', '퍼 주세요'처럼 활용해요. 예전에 쌀을 담아 두던 큰 항아리는 '쌀독'이라고 해요. 쌀을 보관하는 말로 '쌀통에 보관하다'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: The verb for scooping rice is '푸다', which changes to '퍼요' and '퍼 주세요'. The large jar traditionally used to store rice is called a '쌀독'. '쌀통에 보관하다' (store in the rice bin) is a common phrase.

examples.ko: 고기를 상추에 싸서 쌈장을 올려 먹어요.
examples.en: I wrap the meat in lettuce and eat it with ssamjang on top.
The ssamjang my mom makes is the best.
I added a little minced garlic to the ssamjang.

examples.ko: 쌈장은 짤 수 있으니 조금만 찍으세요.
examples.en: Ssamjang can be salty, so dip just a little.
Fresh vegetables dipped in ssamjang taste good.
I asked the pork belly restaurant for more ssamjang.

explain: '쌈'과 같이 외우면 쉬워요. 상추쌈, 깻잎쌈처럼 쌈 채소에 밥과 고기를 올리고 쌈장을 조금 얹어 먹어요. '쌈장을 찍다, 바르다, 올리다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Learn it with '쌈' (a wrap). You put rice and meat on a leaf such as lettuce or perilla, as in '상추쌈' and '깻잎쌈', and add a little ssamjang. You say '쌈장을 찍다' (dip), '바르다' (spread) or '올리다' (put on top).

examples.en: On a really hot day, iced coffee is the best.
One iced coffee here, please.
Please don't put syrup in the iced coffee.
I drink iced coffee even in cold winter.
The iced coffee was too weak, so I added a shot.
Iced coffee tastes watery once the ice melts.

explain: 카페에서는 '아이스 아메리카노'를 줄여 친구끼리 '아아'라고도 해요. 반대로 뜨거운 커피는 '따뜻한 커피'나 '핫커피'라고 말해요. 주문할 때는 '아이스로 주세요'처럼 줄여 말해도 돼요.
explain_en: At cafes, friends shorten '아이스 아메리카노' to '아아'. The opposite is '따뜻한 커피' or '핫커피'. When ordering, you can also say just '아이스로 주세요' (iced, please).

examples.en: My glasses lenses are cloudy, so I can't see well.
I fell on the stairs and my lens cracked.

examples.ko: 안경알을 닦을 때는 부드러운 천을 쓰세요.
examples.en: Use a soft cloth when you wipe your lenses.

examples.ko: 안경점에서 테는 그대로 두고 안경알만 바꿨어요.
examples.en: At the optician's I kept the frame and changed only the lenses.
My prescription is strong, so the lenses are thick.
I got rained on, and water drops formed on my lenses.

explain: 안경 전체는 '안경', 틀은 '안경테'라고 해요. 안경점에서는 '렌즈'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '안경알'도 많이 써요. '안경알을 닦다·바꾸다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: The whole pair is '안경' and the frame is '안경테'. At an optician's you may also hear '렌즈', but in daily life '안경알' is commonly used. You say '안경알을 닦다' (wipe) or '바꾸다' (replace).

examples.en: The front door of the shop is locked, so please come to the back door.

examples.ko: 택배 기사님이 앞문 앞에 상자를 두고 가셨어요.
examples.en: The delivery driver left the box in front of the front door.
The front door was broken, so I went in through the back door.

examples.ko: 수업이 시작되자 교실 앞문으로 선생님이 들어오셨어요.
examples.en: When class began, the teacher came in through the front door of the classroom.
A seat near the front door on the subway is empty.

examples.ko: 차 앞문을 열고 아이를 먼저 태웠어요.
examples.en: I opened the front door of the car and put the child in first.

explain: 반대말은 '뒷문'이고, 교실이나 버스처럼 앞뒤에 문이 있는 곳에서 많이 써요. 학교나 건물의 '정문'은 정식 출입구를 가리켜서 '앞문'과 항상 같지는 않아요. '앞문으로 들어가다, 앞문으로 나가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '뒷문' (back door), and it is common in places with doors at both ends, like classrooms and buses. A school or building's '정문' (main gate) is the official entrance and is not always the same as the '앞문'. You say '앞문으로 들어가다/나가다' (go in/out through the front door).

examples.ko: 앞일은 아무도 모르니까 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: No one knows what lies ahead, so don't worry too much.
When I think about what's ahead, I can't sleep.
He invested while looking far ahead into the future.
The future felt hopeless, so I talked it over with my parents yesterday.

examples.ko: 졸업하고 나서 앞일을 같이 의논해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's discuss what comes next together after we graduate.
You can think about what's next when the time comes.

explain: '미래'보다 일상적인 말이고, 내가 앞으로 겪을 일을 걱정하거나 기대할 때 써요. '앞일이 걱정되다, 앞일을 내다보다, 앞일을 알 수 없다'처럼 짝이 되는 표현이 많아요. 지나간 일은 '지난 일'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is more everyday than '미래' (future) and is used when you worry about or look forward to what you will go through. Common pairings are '앞일이 걱정되다', '앞일을 내다보다' and '앞일을 알 수 없다'. Things that have already passed are '지난 일'.

examples.ko: 우리 집 화장실에 양변기를 새로 설치했어요.
examples.en: We installed a new toilet in our bathroom.
The toilet got clogged, so I called a repairman.
Water keeps trickling in the toilet.
Clean the inside of the toilet thoroughly with a brush.

examples.ko: 옛날 집에는 양변기가 없는 곳도 많았어요.
examples.en: Many old houses didn't have a sit-down toilet.

examples.ko: 양변기에 휴지 말고 다른 건 버리지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't throw anything but toilet paper into the toilet.

explain: 앉아서 쓰는 서양식 변기를 말하고, '좌변기'라고도 해요. 옛날식 화장실의 쪼그려 앉는 변기와 구분할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '변기'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the Western-style sit-down toilet and is also called '좌변기'. It is used to tell it apart from old-style squat toilets. In daily life people also just say '변기'.

examples.en: How on earth did you hurt your leg like that?
How did you end up becoming friends with that person?
I hear from him once in a while.
I accidentally deleted the file by mistake.
I happened to run into an old friend on the street.
How did you end up this late today?

explain: 질문에서 '어쩌다가 ~했어요?'라고 하면 어떻게 그런 일이 생겼는지 놀라거나 걱정하며 묻는 말이에요. 평서문에서는 '우연히'나 '가끔'에 가까워서 '어쩌다가 한 번'처럼 써요. 줄여서 '어쩌다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: In a question, '어쩌다가 ~했어요?' asks how something came about, often with surprise or concern. In a statement it is close to 'by chance' or 'occasionally', as in '어쩌다가 한 번' (once in a while). It is often shortened to '어쩌다'.

examples.en: One glass of ice water here, please.
After exercising, I gulped down ice water.

examples.ko: 얼음물에 손을 담그니 정신이 번쩍 들어요.
examples.en: Dipping my hand in ice water makes me snap awake.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 얼음물을 보온병에 담아 다녀요.
examples.en: On hot days, I carry ice water in a thermos.
Ice water is so cold that it hurts my teeth.
I soaked a towel in ice water and put it on my forehead.

explain: '찬물'은 그냥 차가운 물이고, '얼음물'은 얼음이 들어 있는 물이에요. 식당에서는 차가운 물을 '냉수'라고 부르는 곳도 있어요. 따뜻한 물은 '따뜻한 물'이나 '온수'라고 해요.
explain_en: '찬물' is simply cold water, while '얼음물' has ice in it. Some restaurants call cold water '냉수'. Warm water is '따뜻한 물' or '온수'.

examples.ko: 다리를 다쳐서 친구 등에 업혀 갔어요.
examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I got carried on my friend's back.

examples.ko: 아기가 엄마 등에 업혀서 새근새근 자요.
examples.en: The baby sleeps soundly on its mother's back.

examples.ko: 아이가 피곤한지 아빠에게 업히고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child must be tired, since he wants to be carried on Dad's back.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할아버지 등에 업힌 기억이 아직 나요.
examples.en: I still remember being carried on Grandpa's back when I was little.
I'm heavy, so I feel bad about getting a piggyback from my friend.

examples.ko: 산에서 내려올 때 동생이 형한테 업혀 왔어요.
examples.en: Coming down the mountain, the younger brother was carried on his older brother's back.

explain: '업다'는 등에 지는 쪽, '업히다'는 등에 올라타는 쪽이에요. '엄마가 아기를 업어요'와 '아기가 엄마에게 업혀요'처럼 조사도 바뀌어요. 같은 짝으로 '안다'와 '안기다'도 있어요.
explain_en: '업다' is for the person who carries someone on their back, and '업히다' is for the one being carried. The particles change too: '엄마가 아기를 업어요' (Mom carries the baby) versus '아기가 엄마에게 업혀요' (the baby is carried by Mom). '안다' (hold in arms) and '안기다' (be held) are a similar pair.

examples.en: On the weekend, I bought cool summer clothes at the market.

examples.ko: 여름옷은 땀이 잘 마르는 소재를 고르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For summer clothes, it's good to choose fabric that dries sweat well.

examples.ko: 겨울이 지나면 옷장에 있는 여름옷부터 꺼내요.
examples.en: When winter passes, I take summer clothes out of the closet first.
My summer clothes are thin, so the air conditioning feels cold.
The price of summer clothes has gone up a lot since last year.

examples.ko: 휴가 갈 때 여름옷 몇 벌만 챙기세요.
examples.en: When you go on vacation, just pack a few summer outfits.

explain: 계절별로 '봄옷, 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷'처럼 말해요. 철이 바뀔 때 옷을 바꿔 정리하는 걸 '옷 정리를 하다'라고 해요. 옷은 '벌'로 세서 '여름옷 세 벌'이라고 해요.
explain_en: By season you say '봄옷, 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷'. When the season changes, swapping out your wardrobe is '옷 정리를 하다'. Clothes are counted with '벌', as in '여름옷 세 벌'.

en: women's section of a public bath house

examples.en: On Sunday I went to the women's bath with my mom.
Excuse me, where is the entrance to the women's bath?
The women's bath is on the right and the men's is on the left.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 아빠는 남탕, 저는 여탕에 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, Dad went to the men's bath and I went to the women's.

examples.ko: 이 목욕탕 여탕에는 작은 사우나도 있어요.
examples.en: The women's side of this bathhouse also has a small sauna.
The women's bath was quiet today, so I washed comfortably.

explain: '남탕'과 짝이 되는 말로, 대중목욕탕 입구에서 많이 보여요. 말로 풀어서 '여자 목욕탕'이라고 하기도 해요. '여탕에 가다'처럼 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 목욕탕 이야기를 할 때만 나와요.
explain_en: It pairs with '남탕' (men's bath) and is commonly seen at the entrance of public bathhouses. It can also be spelled out as '여자 목욕탕'. You say '여탕에 가다', and it mostly comes up when talking about bathhouses.

examples.ko: 휴가를 위해 여행용 가방을 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new travel bag for the vacation.
A travel toothbrush set is convenient to have.
This shampoo is for travel, so it is small.
I put my cosmetics in a small travel pouch.

examples.ko: 여행용으로 쓰기에 이 카메라는 가벼워서 좋아요.
examples.en: This camera is light, so it is good for travel use.
I forgot to pack the travel charger.

explain: '-용'은 '쓰임'을 나타내는 말로 앞말에 붙여 써요. '학생용, 어린이용, 업무용'처럼 같은 방식으로 많이 써요. '여행용 가방'처럼 뒤에 명사가 오거나 '여행용이에요'처럼 끝에 올 수 있어요.
explain_en: The suffix '-용' marks what something is for and is attached directly to the preceding word, as in '학생용' (for students), '어린이용' (for kids) and '업무용' (for work). It can come before a noun, like '여행용 가방', or at the end of a sentence, like '여행용이에요'.

examples.en: Wearing a light purple dress makes you look bright.
The curtains in my room are a soft light purple.
Light purple flowers bloom a lot in spring.
What colors go well with light purple?

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 친구가 연보라색 우산을 빌려줬어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day, my friend lent me a light purple umbrella.
The sky turned light purple because of the sunset.

explain: '연-'은 색 이름 앞에 붙어 '연한' 느낌을 줘요. 같은 방식으로 '연분홍', '연노랑'도 있어요. 말할 때는 '색'을 빼고 '연보라 원피스'라고도 해요.
explain_en: The prefix '연-' before a color name gives a light, pale feel. The same pattern gives '연분홍' (light pink) and '연노랑' (light yellow). In speech you can drop '색' and say '연보라 원피스'.

examples.ko: 저희 부모님은 대학에서 만나 연애결혼을 하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents met at university and had a love marriage.

examples.ko: 저는 소개로 만나는 것보다 연애결혼이 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer a love marriage to meeting through an introduction.
I heard that in the old days few people had love marriages.
Even couples who had a love marriage sometimes argue a lot.

examples.ko: 연애결혼이든 소개로 만나든 서로 맞추는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: Whether you had a love marriage or met through an introduction, adjusting to each other matters.
After dating for three years, they had a love marriage.

explain: 서로 사귀다가 결혼하는 걸 말하고, 반대는 '중매결혼'이에요. 소개로 만나 결혼하는 경우는 '맞선을 보고 결혼했다'처럼 말하기도 해요. '연애결혼을 하다'와 '연애결혼하다' 둘 다 써요.
explain_en: It means dating first and then marrying, and the opposite is '중매결혼' (arranged marriage). For meeting through an introduction you may hear '맞선을 보고 결혼했다' (married after a formal matchmaking meeting). Both '연애결혼을 하다' and '연애결혼하다' are used.

examples.ko: 고등학생 때 연애편지를 처음 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote a love letter for the first time in high school.
An old love letter turned up in the desk drawer.
I wrote a love letter all night and my face turned red.
These days people send messages instead of love letters.

examples.ko: 그는 매일 밤 연애편지를 한 장씩 썼대요.
examples.en: I heard he wrote one love letter every night.
The handwriting in the love letter is so pretty.

explain: '러브레터'라고도 하지만 일상 대화에서는 '연애편지'를 많이 써요. '연애편지를 쓰다, 보내다, 받다'처럼 말해요. 손으로 쓴 편지는 '손편지'라고 해요.
explain_en: '러브레터' is also used, but in everyday talk '연애편지' is common. You say '연애편지를 쓰다/보내다/받다' (write/send/receive). A handwritten letter is called a '손편지'.

examples.en: The child sharpened the pencil to a point with a pencil sharpener.
The pencil sharpener broke, so I sharpened it with a knife.
I put a small pencil sharpener on the desk.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 연필깎이 앞에서 연필을 깎았어요.
examples.en: The day before the exam, I sharpened pencils at the sharpener.
The pencil sharpener is full of pencil shavings.
I bought a portable pencil sharpener at the stationery store.

explain: 발음은 [연필까끼]예요. '연필을 깎다'에서 나온 말이라서 도구를 나타내는 '-이'가 붙었어요. 칼로 깎을 때는 '연필을 깎다'라고만 해요.
explain_en: It is pronounced [연필까끼]. It comes from '연필을 깎다' (sharpen a pencil), with '-이' added to name the tool. If you do it with a knife, you simply say '연필을 깎다'.

examples.ko: 사진 속 아버지의 옆모습이 저랑 닮았어요.
examples.en: My father's profile in the photo looks like mine.
That actor's profile is really handsome.
I drew a side view of my friend sitting by the window.
I can tell who it is just from the profile, even from far away.
I checked my side view in the mirror.
When you smile, your profile is just like Mom's.

explain: '앞모습', '뒷모습'과 같이 외우면 쉬워요. 얼굴만 가리킬 때는 '옆얼굴'이라고도 해요. 사람의 분위기를 말할 때 '뒷모습'처럼 '옆모습'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Learn it alongside '앞모습' (front view) and '뒷모습' (back view). When you mean just the face, you can say '옆얼굴'. Like '뒷모습', '옆모습' is also used to talk about how a person looks or comes across.

examples.en: Stand the umbrella up beside the door.
It's faster if you take the side road.
There's a small chair on the side of the bookshelf.
If you go around the side of the building, you'll find the parking lot.
May I sit in the seat over there on the side?
I was startled when a car suddenly came out from the side.

explain: '옆'은 바로 곁을 가리키고, '옆쪽'은 그 방향이나 조금 넓은 범위를 말할 때 어울려요. '앞쪽, 뒤쪽, 옆쪽'처럼 방향을 나타내는 말과 같이 외우면 좋아요. 길을 설명할 때 '옆쪽으로 돌아가세요'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '옆' points to what is right beside you, while '옆쪽' fits the direction or a somewhat wider area. Learn it with '앞쪽' and '뒤쪽' (front side, back side). When giving directions, say things like '옆쪽으로 돌아가세요' (go around the side).

examples.en: The exam is today or tomorrow, so I'm nervous all the time.
I'll check and get back to you within today or tomorrow.
I heard it will keep raining today and tomorrow.
I'm a bit busy today and tomorrow because I have appointments.

examples.ko: 이 책은 오늘내일 안에 다 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can finish this book within a day or two.
They said the package I ordered will arrive today or tomorrow.

explain: '오늘이나 내일'을 한 단어처럼 붙여서 아주 가까운 때를 말해요. 정확한 날짜를 모르지만 곧이라는 느낌이라 '오늘내일 중으로'를 자주 써요. 더 넓게 말하려면 '이삼일'이나 '요 며칠'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The baby's due date is near, so it could be any day now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 큰일이 일어날 것 같을 때 써요. 출산처럼 기다리는 일이 임박했을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something important is about to happen very soon, such as waiting on a baby's birth.

explain_en: It joins 'today or tomorrow' into one word to mean a very near time. It suggests 'very soon' without a firm date, so '오늘내일 중으로' (within today or tomorrow) is common. For a wider span, say '이삼일' (two or three days) or '요 며칠' (these few days).

examples.en: I left this neighborhood a long time ago.

examples.ko: 한국에서는 집에 들어갈 때 신발을 벗는 풍습이 오래전부터 있었어요.
examples.en: In Korea, the custom of taking off shoes when entering a home has existed since long ago.
It was so long ago that I can't remember the name.
It was long ago, but it's still vivid.
I reread a novel I had read long ago.
I took an old photo out of the album and looked at it.

explain: 한 단어이므로 '오래전'처럼 붙여 쓰고, 조사는 '오래전에, 오래전부터, 오래전의'로 이어져요. '옛날'은 훨씬 먼 과거나 이야기 속 시대에 어울리고, '오래전'은 몇 년이나 몇십 년 전처럼 내가 아는 과거에 써요. 반대로 가까운 과거는 '얼마 전', '최근'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is written as one word, '오래전', and takes particles as in '오래전에', '오래전부터' and '오래전의'. '옛날' suits a much farther past or storybook times, while '오래전' fits a past you personally know, such as years or decades ago. The recent past is '얼마 전' or '최근'.

examples.ko: 올가을에는 설악산 단풍을 보러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: This fall I'm going to see the autumn leaves at Seoraksan.
The weather this fall is unusually clear and cool.
Where would be a good family trip destination this fall?
I started taking Korean classes this fall.

examples.ko: 올가을 단풍은 예년만큼 곱지 않다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the autumn leaves this fall aren't as beautiful as usual.

examples.ko: 올가을은 일이 많아서 여행 갈 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: I have so much work this fall that I have no time to travel.

explain: '올해 가을'을 짧게 말한 거예요. 같은 방식으로 '올봄, 올여름, 올겨울'이 있고, 지난해는 '지난가을'처럼 말해요. '이번 가을'도 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a short way of saying 'this year's fall'. The same pattern gives '올봄', '올여름' and '올겨울', and last year's is '지난가을'. '이번 가을' can be used in a similar way.

examples.en: This winter there is more snow than last year.
The cold this winter is severe, and the water pipes froze.
This winter I want to try learning to ski.
I bought a padded jacket in advance for this winter.
I'm worried about how big the heating bill will be this winter.

examples.ko: 올겨울이 끝나면 새집으로 이사를 갈 거예요.
examples.en: When this winter is over, we're going to move to a new house.

explain: '올해 겨울'을 줄인 말이고, 지금 겨울이거나 곧 올 겨울을 가리켜요. 지난해 겨울은 '지난겨울'이라고 해요. '올봄, 올여름, 올가을'과 같은 방식으로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a shortened '올해 겨울' and points to the winter happening now or coming soon. Last year's winter is '지난겨울'. It follows the same pattern as '올봄', '올여름' and '올가을'.

examples.ko: 올봄에는 벚꽃 구경을 꼭 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: This spring I definitely want to go see the cherry blossoms.
The fine dust this spring wasn't as bad as last year.
This spring I finally found a new job.
I've been jogging every morning since this spring.

examples.ko: 올봄은 비가 자주 와서 꽃이 일찍 졌어요.
examples.en: It rained often this spring, so the flowers fell early.

examples.ko: 올봄 졸업 사진을 찍으러 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to school to take graduation photos this spring.

explain: '올여름', '올가을', '올겨울'처럼 한 단어로 붙여 써요. 지난해 봄은 '지난봄', 다음 해 봄은 '내년 봄'이라고 해요. '올봄에는'처럼 계획이나 바람을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is written as one word, like '올여름', '올가을' and '올겨울'. Last year's spring is '지난봄' and next year's is '내년 봄'. It often appears as '올봄에는' when talking about plans or hopes.

examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
This time I'll buy you a nice meal.
This exam was much easier than the last one.
I decided to cut spending this month.
Please help me just this once.
It was a pity that it rained on this trip.

explain: '이번'을 더 말랑하게 말하는 구어체예요. 친한 사이의 대화에서 자연스럽고, 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '이번'이 더 맞아요. 반대로 지나간 때는 '지난번', 다음은 '다음번'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a softer, spoken version of '이번'. It sounds natural among friends, while '이번' fits writing and formal situations better. The previous one is '지난번' and the next one is '다음번'.

examples.en: The weather has suddenly gotten quite chilly lately.
I haven't been sleeping well lately.
Has something good been happening to you lately?

examples.ko: 요사이 회사 일이 많아서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: I have so much work these days that I'm swamped.
I haven't heard anything from my friends lately.
I started exercising lately and my body feels lighter.

explain: '요즘', '요새'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '요새'는 '요사이'를 줄인 말이에요. 문장 맨 앞에서 '요사이 어때요?'처럼 안부를 물을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '요즘' and '요새'; '요새' is the contracted form of '요사이'. You can put it at the start of a sentence to ask how someone is, as in '요사이 어때요?'.
